_README: Why a stage has no results, for stages where the absence is PERMANENT and correct.
Purpose: stop the same stage being re-investigated and re-scraped. A stage with
cancelled=1 and zero results looks identical to a stage nobody has gotten around to
scraping yet, and there is nothing in the row itself to tell the two apart.
Keyed by races.name -> year -> stages.stage_number (the DB's contiguous integer).
'slug' records the PCS source_slug alongside it because the two diverge on any
edition with a split day: Giro 1946 DB stage 14 is PCS stage-12, Giro 1969 DB stage
21 is PCS stage-20. Never rebuild a PCS URL from stage_number.
Only stages with a verified reason are listed. validate_db.py reports cancelled
stages that are still undocumented rather than inventing an explanation for them.

21.note: STAGE 20 (not 21 — DB stage_number 21 is the internal integer; the 18a/18b split day on 3 June puts it one ahead of the official number from stage 19 onward). Scheduled Thursday 5 June 1969 and cancelled because of bad weather, confirmed by both bikeraceinfo and PCS. No classification was recorded, so no result exists to scrape and none ever will. DO NOT re-scrape. The stage was stored with the WRONG date (1969-06-04, duplicating stage 19's) until 2026-08-15, which made the app render it as a phantom split day '19b' and shifted every later label down one, so the finale showed as 22 instead of 23.
21.source: https://www.bikeraceinfo.com/giro/giro1969.html ('Thursday, June 5: Stage 20, Trento - Marmolada. Stage 20 canceled because of bad weather') and https://www.procyclingstats.com/race/giro-d-italia/1969/stage-20/result/result — Eric, 2026-08-15

18.note: Cancelled in the aftermath of the San Remo anti-doping raids. No classification was recorded.

4.note: Neutralized to honor Wouter Weylandt, whose death in a crash on stage 3 shook the entire cycling world. The stage was ridden as a processional tribute, with Weylandt's Leopard Trek teammates leading the peloton across the line together. No times and no classification were taken, so PCS publishes no result and none exists to find. DO NOT re-scrape. Its real distance (about 216 km) is consequently absent from the edition's summed total, and accounts for the whole of Giro 2011's -4.9% distance divergence against Wikipedia — see distance_divergence_baseline.json.

19.note: Cancelled: adverse weather on the Gavia and Stelvio. No classification was recorded.
